newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Low rouble demand cuts Russian yields, rouble rate.
newsitem.headline: Low rouble demand cuts Russian yields, rouble rate.

text.p: Weaker demand for the Russian rouble pushed the dollar and GKO discount Treasury bill prices up on Friday, dealers said.
They said T-bill yields fell to the customary level of 19 percent, while steady demand showed that Thursday's fall in yields was a short-term reaction to high yields at Wednesday's auctions.
*Average yield on taxable T-bills fell to 18.97 pct from 19.38 pct on Thursday
*Average yield on taxable floating rate bonds was 31.64 pct after 32.15 pct
*Turnover fell to 3.87 trln rbls from 4.56 trln rbls

"Yesterday, we saw yields that were way too good, but today, we are sure of tomorrow," said Renaissance Capital dealer Alexei Orekhov. "On seeing the 19.5 percent yield, a lot of people realised it is unwise to wish for more, and they started buying."
Dealers said the market was stable, with the resistance level of 19.0 percent firm.
On the foreign exchange market, overnight credit rates fell to their usual levels, while the dollar rose, a dealer said.
"The day was quiet, the market calm," he said.
